summary: Unplanned routing to degraded inference variant during traffic surge causing elevated p95/p99 and request timeouts
description:
Issue summary:
During a customer traffic surge on 2026-03-12 evening, requests from BrightHealthAI started timing out and experienced elevated p95/p99 latency. Investigation shows a subset of requests were routed to a degraded/older quantized variant that has higher cold-start latency and lower throughput. The routing decision appears to have been triggered by autoscaling signals combined with a short-lived capacity constraint in the primary pool.

Impact:
- Multiple API calls returning 504s for 10-20% of user requests over a 40-minute window.
- Customer reports production errors and observed timeouts in their user-facing inference feature.
- Billing spike risk due to repeated retries from the client (they retried twice before giving up).

Environment:
- Redwood prod (us-east primary) serving BrightHealthAI dedicated capacity pool.
- Traffic spike originated at 2026-03-12T18:32:00Z.
- Primary model pinned: redwood/rlhf-vicuna-13b (pinned at v2026-02-08).
- Fallback variant observed: redwood/quant-13b-q4 (legacy quantized variant without pre-warm pool).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send sustained burst of 120 concurrent requests targeting /v1/generate with the pinned model for ~5 minutes.
2) Observe routing decisions in response headers: x-redwood-variant and x-redwood-routing-reason.
3) On surge, a subset of responses have x-redwood-variant: redwood/quant-13b-q4 and show significantly higher latency or 504s.

Observed behavior / Logs:
- Router logs show fallback routing reason: "capacity_unavailable" then "compatible_variant" between 2026-03-12T18:33:10Z and 2026-03-12T19:10:00Z.
- Serving runtime logs indicate repeated cold starts for quant-13b-q4 (avg cold start 3.2s) and queue growth to >250 pending requests on some workers.
- Autoscaler fired up additional instances but the warmup policy did not pre-load KV caches for the quant variant.
- Customer-side retry pattern amplified load; retries with short backoff (200-500ms) worsened tail latency.

Initial hypothesis:
- Smart-routing policy selected a compatible but degraded variant when the primary pool experienced transient capacity pressure. The degraded variant lacks warm pools and has higher cold-start time, which combined with customer retries produced elevated p95/p99 and timeouts.
- A mismatch between autoscaler warmup heuristics and variant capability (quantized variant not eligible for warm pool) allowed cold-starts to dominate.

Temporary mitigation applied (03/12 19:02Z):
- Support toggled routing policy for BrightHealthAI to strict model pinning to prevent fallback to legacy quant variant (implemented via per-customer routing override).
- Recommended customer increase client-side retry backoff to exponential with jitter (support note sent).

Next steps (owner: serving-runtime / smart-routing):
- Verify and patch routing decision logic to prefer warmable variants when available and avoid legacy quant variants unless explicitly pinned. (ENG-3124)
- Add telemetry that records whether a routed variant has warm-pool capability and expose in router response headers. (ENG-3140)
- Evaluate adding an autoscaling pre-warm hook for newly created instances serving quantized variants or disallow routing to variants without warm pools under high-QPS scenarios.
- Coordinate with Customer Success to confirm recovery and update runbook for fallback routing during capacity spikes.

Follow-up communications:
- CS updated BrightHealthAI on the routing override and recommended client changes at 2026-03-12T19:20Z.
- Engineering notified on #incidents and assigned ENG-3124 and ENG-3140 for fixes.

investigation_notes: Key signals: router fallbacks correlated tightly with transient capacity pressure in dedicated pool. Quantized legacy variant lacked warm-pool capability, exposing cold-starts under load. Autoscaler created instances but warmup semantics differ per-variant. Need code-level guardrails in smart-routing to avoid routing to non-warm variants when latency SLOs are at risk. Also add per-customer circuit to prevent routing to legacy variants if customer is on dedicated pool.
resolution: Partial mitigation: per-customer routing override enforced to honor primary model pinning and prevent fallback to legacy quantized variant. Customer updated client retry policy. Engineering to deliver routing policy changes and telemetry in ENG-3124 / ENG-3140. Post-incident review scheduled.
